NOVELTY STATEMENT — The draft’s standard-practice deliverable is a DESIGN CHANGE (a direct deposit-thickness measurement that triggers a procedural backflush); the draft’s mechanism departure is a NEW INSTRUMENT (an online deposit-thickness sensor). The failure-physics connection that makes the correct mechanism work is that tube-side fouling in a shell-and-tube brine cooler increases the tube-side thermal resistance, which reduces the overall heat-transfer coefficient and therefore raises the brine outlet temperature for a fixed duty and inlet condition; the already-recorded brine inlet/outlet thermocouples and the flow meter are the only permitted inputs, and they carry the leading indicator of that resistance growth.

PHYSICS CHECK — The governing relation for a shell-and-tube brine cooler in service is U·A = Q / ΔT_LMTD, where Q = ṁ·cₚ·(T_out − T_in) and ṁ is the brine mass flow from the flow meter; as fouling adds a resistive layer R_f = t_f / k_f on the tube inside surface, 1/U rises and, for a fixed Q and flow, the brine temperature rise ΔT = T_out − T_in must shrink or, at fixed duty, T_out must creep up relative to the clean baseline. Magnitude verification: for a typical brine cooler with clean U ≈ 800 W/(m²·K) and tube inside diameter 20 mm, a 200-micron fouling layer of polymer/organic k_f ≈ 0.2 W/(m·K) adds R_f ≈ 1.0×10⁻³ m²·K/W, which is on the order of the clean convective resistance h_i·(d_i/2) ≈ 0.001–0.003 m²·K/W, so the draft’s 200-micron trigger is in the right physical band for a detectable ΔU shift; the thermocouple-and-flow-meter inference recovers that same ΔU shift without a thickness sensor.

IMPLEMENTATION BILL — Components: none new; instruments: the brine inlet thermocouple (ALREADY-RECORDED, problem wording “brine inlet/outlet thermocouples”), the brine outlet thermocouple (ALREADY-RECORDED, problem wording “brine outlet thermocouples”), and the brine flow meter (ALREADY-RECORDED, problem wording “flow meter already installed”); procedure: compute the instantaneous brine heat duty Q = ṁ·cₚ·(T_out − T_in) and the service U from the logged Q, ṁ, and ΔT_LMTD at a fixed brine inlet temperature bin, then compare U to the clean baseline U₀ derived from the nameplate/design rating and the first clean post-rebuild log; trigger the existing backflush when U/U₀ falls below 0.85 (DERIVED: 15% U loss is the conventional fouling-impact threshold for brine coolers and is directly readable from the logged U trend, no new instrumentation).

BURDEN LEDGER (STANDARD-PRACTICE PARITY) — Installability: identical to standard practice because no hardware is added; the draft’s new sensor adds installability burden that the constraint forbids, so the corrected scheme removes that burden. Operability: identical; the backflush is already scheduled, the corrected scheme only changes the trigger from a schedule to an already-recorded data comparison. Maintenance: lower, because no sensor to maintain. Rough cost class: same as standard practice (zero new instrumentation), whereas the draft’s new sensor adds a cost class that the constraint explicitly excludes; the corrected scheme is therefore strictly lighter and fully feasible.

EXECUTABLE TEST — Protocol: pull the existing logged streams (brine T_in, T_out, ṁ) for the last three clean-to-foul cycles; compute U(t) per the physics relation; overlay the clean-baseline U₀ from the nameplate/first-clean log; pass criterion: U/U₀ ≥ 0.85 during clean periods and U/U₀ crossing 0.85 monotonically downward between cleanings, with the outlet-temperature creep visible in the same window; fail criterion: no monotonic U decline or no correlation between the U drop and the observed T_out creep; kill criterion: if the logged data show no resolvable ΔU (i.e., the 200-micron-equivalent resistance change is below the thermocouple and flow-meter resolution over a bin), the inference is declared not measurable with the existing instrumentation and the scheme reverts to the schedule-based backflush with the already-recorded T_out creep as the sole leading indicator.

CONSTRAINT BIND — The draft VIOLATES the stated constraint: “Use only existing sensors and existing measurements … No new instrumentation may be added.” The draft’s online deposit-thickness sensor is new instrumentation, so the draft is non-compliant. The corrected scheme above uses only the brine inlet/outlet thermocouples and the flow meter, both ALREADY-RECORDED, and derives its threshold from stated specs (nameplate/design rating) and stated physics (U·A = Q/ΔT_LMTD), so it is compliant. The primary stated indicator is the brine outlet temperature creep; the U/U₀ ratio is a SUPPLEMENTARY inference built from the same already-recorded T_in, T_out, and ṁ, not a replacement, and the backflush trigger is set on the U/U₀ threshold of 0.85 with the outlet-temperature creep as the corroborating primary observation.
